question: Which of the following is NOT a food preservative?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Aqua regia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aqua regia,** a potent liquid, is characterized by its corrosive, acidic, and oxidative properties, resulting from a blend of hydrochloric acid and nitric acid.
 
• Its chemical formula, HNO₃+3 HCl, reflects the mixture with a standard ratio of three parts hydrochloric acid to one part nitric acid. Initially, aqua regia appears fuming and colorless, but it swiftly transforms into hues of yellow, orange, or red upon preparation.
 
• This solution finds widespread application in metallurgy, where it effectively dissolves metals such as gold and platinum, either for analytical purposes or to eliminate trace contaminants.
 
• Furthermore, aqua regia serves as a crucial agent in glassware cleaning procedures and plays a pivotal role in gold refining processes.
 
• The name "aqua regia" originates from the Latin term "royal water," denoting its unique ability to dissolve noble metals like gold and platinum, traditionally associated with royalty. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Food preservatives **play a crucial role in preventing food spoilage caused by microbial growth, thereby extending the shelf life of various food products and ensuring their safety.
 
• Commonly used food preservatives include sugar, table salt, vegetable oil, and sodium benzoate.
 
• Salt, for instance, is employed to inhibit microbial growth in vegetables and meats, effectively preserving their freshness.
 
• Additionally, sorbic acid and propanoic acid salts are widely utilized as preservatives, further enhancing the stability and safety of food products.
 
• These preservatives help to control the growth of bacteria and other microorganisms, thereby maintaining the quality and integrity of the food.
